paper_metadata.title: Synthetic data generation with hybrid quantum-classical models for the financial sector

summary: The paper evaluates a hybrid quantum–classical GAN using a 5‑qubit quantum generator (4 data qubits + 1 ancilla) with 30 trainable parameters on a simulator to generate synthetic financial data from a dataset of over 13 million records (54,490 minority-class samples). Compared with a classical GAN (805,600‑parameter generator), the HQGAN shows unstable training and consistently higher MSE, failing to match the classical model’s performance.

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical GAN for synthetic financial data generation, using a quantum circuit as the generator and a classical neural network discriminator, compared against a fully classical GAN baseline.

algorithm.variant: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Generative Adversarial Network (HQGAN) with quantum generator and classical discriminator
algorithm.ansatz: Angle embedding with Ry rotations plus parameterized ansatz layers with linear entanglement via controlled-Z gates
algorithm.convergence_criteria: trained for 5449 epochs; additional truncated run at approximately 2500 iterations to inspect divergence

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical features are normalized to [0,1] and encoded into qubit rotation angles using Ry; one feature per data qubit, with two padded zero features to fit 2^NG output capacity
problem_formulation.objective_function: Generate synthetic samples matching the real financial-data distribution; evaluated via BCE training loss and MSE distance between synthetic and real data
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: partial measurement and ancilla qubit used to induce nonlinearity; dataset padded with two zero-valued features to match generator output dimensionality

problem_instance.description: Synthetic generation of approved-client financial records for Banco BV FGTS withdrawal approval data
problem_instance.dataset_name: Banco BV FGTS withdrawal approval dataset

dataset_specification.description: April 2022 to July 2022; 16 features originally, with 2 discarded (target and time); one categorical feature ordinal-encoded; features min-max normalized to [0,1]

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: discard target and time features; ordinal encode the single categorical feature; min-max scale all features to [0,1]; pad with two additional zero features for the quantum generator
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: compare HQGAN and classical GAN using loss convergence and MSE distance; additional experiment truncates training at ~2500 iterations to inspect convergence behavior

implementation_details.classical_solver: PyTorch neural network training; quantum simulations executed on Kuatomu quantum simulator
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: ordinal encoding of one categorical feature; min-max normalization; feature padding
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: MSE comparison between generated and real data; loss-curve analysis

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: HQGAN loss initially stable then diverges mid-training; truncated run shows apparent loss convergence but MSE remains erratic

speedup_claims.conditions: The paper compares empirical training behavior and synthetic-data quality only; no speedup analysis is provided.
speedup_claims.caveats: No asymptotic, theoretical, or empirical speedup claim is made. The paper reports that the HQGAN underperforms the classical GAN on MSE and shows unstable training.

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not reported; no complexity analysis or scaling study provided.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Unknown; the paper does not provide asymptotic complexity, logical qubit requirements, or scaling estimates for a quantum advantage.
limiting_factors: Quantum model evaluated only on simulator (no hardware execution)
Erratic training behavior and divergence observed in loss curves
Higher MSE compared to classical GAN throughout training
No complexity or scaling analysis demonstrating advantage

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_other because the paper states simulations were executed on the quantum simulator Kuatomu and no real QPU device is named.
num_qubits reported from the quantum generator design: 4 data qubits + 1 ancilla qubit.
circuit_depth reported as k=1 in the circuit figure/caption; deeper circuits are described as repetitions of the ansatz.
No asymptotic speedup analysis is provided; the paper instead reports empirical performance and notes limitations.
Section 5 concludes that HQGAN 'did not achieve sufficient accuracy to learn the complex patterns present in financial data'.
Figures 4–6 show classical GAN achieving lower MSE and more stable convergence than the hybrid quantum model.
